headings.title: Offense of possessing controlled substances defined
headings.reviewNote: Defines the offense of possession of a controlled substance when a person knowingly possesses a controlled substance without statutory authorization.

headings.title: Class D felony penalty classification
headings.reviewNote: Designates possession of any controlled substance as a class D felony, excluding thirty-five grams or less of marijuana or synthetic cannabinoids.

headings.title: Misdemeanor penalty for intermediate marijuana possession
headings.reviewNote: Classifies possession of more than ten grams but thirty-five grams or less of marijuana or synthetic cannabinoids as a class A misdemeanor.

headings.title: Penalties for small quantity marijuana possession
headings.reviewNote: Classifies possession of ten grams or less of marijuana or any synthetic cannabinoid as a class D misdemeanor, elevated to a class A misdemeanor for prior controlled substance findings of guilt pleaded and proven under section 558.021.

headings.title: Defendant burden of proof for exemptions
headings.reviewNote: Establishes that charging documents need not negative statutory exceptions or exemptions and places the burden of proof upon the defendant.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 subsection headings for 579.015 covering possession offense, class D felony grading, intermediate and small-quantity marijuana/synthetic cannabinoid misdemeanor tiers, and defendant burden of proof (L. 1989 S.B. 215 & 58 through A.L. 2016 H.B. 2332; formerly 195.202; effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Offense of delivery of controlled substances
headings.reviewNote: Defines the offense of delivery of a controlled substance through distribution, delivery, attempt, possession with intent, or permitting minor transport.

headings.title: Class C felony general penalty classification
headings.reviewNote: Designates delivery of a controlled substance as a class C felony, except for thirty-five grams or less of marijuana or minor delivery enhancements.

headings.title: Class E felony for small marijuana delivery
headings.reviewNote: Classifies delivery of thirty-five grams or less of marijuana or synthetic cannabinoids as a class E felony.

headings.title: Class C felony delivery to minor
headings.reviewNote: Upgrades delivery of thirty-five grams or less of marijuana to a class C felony when delivered to a person under seventeen who is at least two years younger.

headings.title: Class B felony enhancements for minor involvement
headings.reviewNote: Designates delivery of other controlled substances to minors or permitting minors to purchase or transport illegal substances as a class B felony.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 subsection headings for 579.020 covering delivery elements, class C felony general grading, class E felony for <=35g marijuana/synthetic cannabinoid, class C felony delivery of <=35g to minors, and class B felony minor enhancements (L. 1989 S.B. 215 & 58, A.L. 2014 S.B. 491; formerly 195.212; effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Delivery of mixed substance causing serious injury
headings.reviewNote: Defines the offense when a person delivers a controlled substance knowing it is mixed with another substance and serious physical injury results.

headings.title: User self-administration not a defense
headings.reviewNote: Establishes that user contribution or consent to administration does not constitute a defense to delivery causing serious physical injury.

headings.title: Class C felony penalty classification
headings.reviewNote: Designates delivery of a controlled substance causing serious physical injury as a class C felony.

headings.title: Controlled substance statutory schedule definition
headings.reviewNote: Restricts the statutory definition of controlled substance for this section to Schedule I and Schedule II substances under section 195.017.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsection headings for 579.021 covering mixed controlled substance delivery causing serious physical injury, user self-administration/consent bar, class C felony grading, and Schedule I/II definition (L. 2024 S.B. 754, et al.).

headings.title: Delivery of controlled substance causing death
headings.reviewNote: Defines the offense of delivery of a controlled substance causing death when a person delivers or distributes a controlled substance under section 579.020 and death results from its use.

headings.title: User self-administration not a defense
headings.reviewNote: Establishes that the user contributing to their own death or consenting to administration does not constitute a defense.

headings.title: Class A felony penalty classification
headings.reviewNote: Designates delivery of a controlled substance causing death as a class A felony.

headings.title: Controlled substance statutory schedule definition
headings.reviewNote: Restricts the statutory definition of controlled substance for this section to Schedule I and Schedule II substances under section 195.017.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsection headings for 579.022 (corrected subsection 1 removing outdated 'mixed substance' element and updated enactment history) covering controlled substance delivery causing death, user self-administration/consent bar, class A felony grading, and Schedule I/II definition (L. 2024 S.B. 754, et al., A.L. 2026 S.B. 1421; severability § 1.1010).

headings.title: Offense of distribution in protected locations
headings.reviewNote: Defines distribution in a protected location (excluding 35 grams or less of marijuana or synthetic cannabinoid) as knowingly distributing, selling, or delivering within 2,000 feet of an elementary, vocational, or secondary school or on a school bus, within 1,000 feet of a park, or in or on public or governmentally assisted housing.

headings.title: Class A felony penalty classification
headings.reviewNote: Designates distribution of a controlled substance in a protected location as a class A felony.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 579.030 (corrected subsection 1 protected location details) covering distribution within 2,000 feet of schools/buses, 1,000 feet of parks, or on public housing (excluding <=35g marijuana/synthetic cannabinoid) and class A felony penalty (L. 1993 S.B. 180 through A.L. 2014 S.B. 491; formerly 195.218; effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Offense of distributing drug paraphernalia defined
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits unlawfully delivering, distributing, or selling drug paraphernalia knowing or reasonably suspecting it will be used with controlled substances.

headings.title: Penalty classification and commercial enhancement
headings.reviewNote: Classifies distributing drug paraphernalia as a class A misdemeanor, elevated to a class E felony if conducted for commercial purposes.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 579.040 covering unlawful distribution, delivery, or sale of drug paraphernalia and class A misdemeanor / commercial class E felony penalties (L. 2014 S.B. 491; effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Definitions of drug masking product and synthetic urine
headings.reviewNote: Defines 'drug masking product' and 'synthetic urine' as substances designated to defraud an alcohol or drug screening test or simulate human urine.

headings.title: Offense of distributing drug masking products
headings.reviewNote: Defines unlawful distribution, delivery, or sale of a drug masking product.

headings.title: Class A misdemeanor penalty classification
headings.reviewNote: Classifies unlawful distribution, delivery, or sale of a drug masking product as a class A misdemeanor.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for 579.041 (rewrote all 3 shifted subsections and corrected enactment citation to L. 2023 S.B. 186) covering definitions of drug masking product and synthetic urine, unlawful distribution offense, and class A misdemeanor penalty.

headings.title: Offense of fraudulently attempting to obtain substances
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits obtaining or attempting to obtain controlled substances through fraud, deceit, misrepresentation, forgery, or false prescription orders.

headings.title: Class E felony penalty classification
headings.reviewNote: Classifies fraudulently attempting to obtain a controlled substance as a class E felony.

headings.title: Physician-patient privilege exception and testimony limits
headings.reviewNote: Provides that information communicated to a physician in an effort to unlawfully procure a controlled substance is not privileged, while preserving incompetence to testify regarding information necessary to prescribe or act as a physician or surgeon.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for 579.045 (rewrote shifted/fabricated subsections 2 and 3) covering fraudulently attempting to obtain a controlled substance, class E felony penalty, and physician-patient privilege exception/testimony limits (L. 1989 S.B. 215 & 58 through A.L. 2014 S.B. 491; formerly 195.204; effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Offense of manufacturing imitation controlled substances
headings.reviewNote: Defines manufacture of an imitation controlled substance as knowingly manufacturing any imitation controlled substance with intent to deliver.

headings.title: Class E felony penalty classification
headings.reviewNote: Designates the manufacture of an imitation controlled substance as a class E felony.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 579.050 covering manufacture of an imitation controlled substance with intent to deliver and class E felony penalty (L. 2014 S.B. 491; effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Offense of manufacturing controlled substances defined
headings.reviewNote: Defines manufacture of a controlled substance as knowingly manufacturing, producing, or growing, attempting to do so, or knowingly possessing a controlled substance with intent to manufacture, produce, or grow.

headings.title: Class B school-zone and class A meth explosion felonies
headings.reviewNote: Classifies manufacturing or attempting to manufacture within 2,000 feet of a school, community college, college, or university as a class B felony, and elevates it to a class A felony if a methamphetamine-production fire or explosion causes serious physical injury or death.

headings.title: Class C felony general penalty classification
headings.reviewNote: Classifies manufacturing or attempting to manufacture any controlled substance, except thirty-five grams or less of marijuana or synthetic cannabinoid, as a class C felony.

headings.title: Class E felony for small marijuana manufacture
headings.reviewNote: Classifies manufacturing thirty-five grams or less of marijuana or synthetic cannabinoid as a class E felony.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsection headings for 579.055 (rewrote shifted/fabricated subsections 2 through 4 and tightened subsection 1 note) covering manufacturing offense, class B school-zone and class A meth fire/explosion enhancements, class C felony general grading, and class E felony for <=35g marijuana (L. 1989 S.B. 215 & 58 through A.L. 2014 S.B. 491; formerly 195.211; effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Precursor quantity, behind-counter, and packaging offenses
headings.reviewNote: Defines offenses for knowingly selling or purchasing ephedrine, phenylpropanolamine, or pseudoephedrine above 7.2g/30 days, 3.6g/24 hours, or 61.2g/12 months without prescription, failing to keep Schedule V products behind a pharmacy counter, or selling nonconforming packages.

headings.title: Pharmacist, intern, and pharmacy technician offenses
headings.reviewNote: Defines offenses by pharmacists, intern pharmacists, or registered pharmacy technicians for selling over 3.6g within 24 hours without prescription, failing to submit sales data or maintain electronic logs, or selling to individuals under eighteen without prescription.

headings.title: Employee training defense for retail owners
headings.reviewNote: Exempts a general owner or operator of a retail outlet from penalty for section 195.418 packaging violations if an employee training program on state and federal precursor regulations is documented.

headings.title: Manufacturer failure to pay required fees
headings.reviewNote: Defines an offense when a manufacturer knowingly fails to pay fees required under section 195.417(7).

headings.title: Class A misdemeanor penalty classification
headings.reviewNote: Classifies unlawful sale, distribution, or purchase of over-the-counter methamphetamine precursor drugs as a class A misdemeanor.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 subsection headings for 579.060 (rewrote fabricated subsections 2–4, corrected subsection 1 and 5 notes, and updated history to 2026) covering general precursor quantity/counter/packaging offenses, pharmacist/technician offenses, owner training defense, manufacturer fee failure, and class A misdemeanor penalty (L. 2014 S.B. 491 through A.L. 2026 H.B. 2372 merged with S.B. 878 & S.B. 1421; severability § 1.1010).

headings.title: Offense of first-degree drug trafficking defined
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits distributing, delivering, manufacturing, or producing controlled substances in quantities exceeding specified threshold amounts.

headings.title: Class B felony penalty classification
headings.reviewNote: Designates trafficking drugs in the first degree as a class B felony for threshold statutory amounts.

headings.title: Class A felony penalty for higher thresholds
headings.reviewNote: Elevates first-degree drug trafficking to a class A felony for higher enumerated quantities (including fentanyl and carfentanil), protected-location stimulant or MDMA trafficking, or repeat flunitrazepam or GHB offenses.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for 579.065 (updated enactment history through A.L. 2026 S.B. 1421 and expanded subsection 3 note) covering first-degree trafficking thresholds (including fentanyl and carfentanil), class B felony grading, and class A felony quantity/location/repeat enhancements (formerly 195.222; severability § 1.1010; cross reference § 544.671).

headings.title: Offense of second-degree drug trafficking defined
headings.reviewNote: Defines second-degree drug trafficking as knowingly possessing, controlling, purchasing, attempting to purchase, or bringing into Missouri enumerated threshold amounts of controlled substances including fentanyl and carfentanil.

headings.title: Class C felony general penalty classification
headings.reviewNote: Designates trafficking drugs in the second degree as a class C felony for primary statutory threshold amounts.

headings.title: Class B felony penalty for intermediate quantities
headings.reviewNote: Elevates second-degree drug trafficking to a class B felony for intermediate statutory quantities of controlled substances.

headings.title: Class A felony penalty for large quantities
headings.reviewNote: Classifies second-degree trafficking as a class A felony for 450 grams or more of amphetamine, methamphetamine, or MDMA.

headings.title: Penalty tiers for flunitrazepam trafficking
headings.reviewNote: Classifies trafficking less than one gram of flunitrazepam as a class C felony for a first offense and class B felony for repeat offenses.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 subsection headings for 579.068 (updated enactment history through A.L. 2026 S.B. 1421) covering second-degree trafficking possession/purchase/importation thresholds, class C, B, and A felony tiers, and flunitrazepam penalties (formerly 195.223; severability § 1.1010).

headings.title: Offense of creating a danger defined
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits setting up booby traps, weapons, or devices intended to cause physical injury while producing controlled substances.

headings.title: Class C felony penalty classification
headings.reviewNote: Designates creating a danger while producing controlled substances as a class C felony.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 579.070 covering protecting drug production with injury-causing devices or weapons and class C felony penalty (L. 1986 S.B. 450, A.L. 2014 S.B. 491; formerly 565.065; effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Offense of furnishing production materials defined
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits providing reagents, solvents, or precursor materials knowing the recipient intends to use them for illegal drug production.

headings.title: Class E felony penalty classification
headings.reviewNote: Designates furnishing materials for the production of a controlled substance as a class E felony.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 579.072 covering furnishing reagents, solvents, or precursor materials knowing of illegal production intent and class E felony penalty (L. 1998 H.B. 1147, et al. § 1, A.L. 2014 S.B. 491; formerly 195.226; effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Offense of possessing drug paraphernalia defined
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits using or possessing with intent to use drug paraphernalia to cultivate, manufacture, test, ingest, or introduce controlled substances.

headings.title: Misdemeanor penalties and repeat offender enhancement
headings.reviewNote: Classifies paraphernalia possession as a class D misdemeanor, enhanced to a class A misdemeanor for prior controlled substance convictions.

headings.title: Class E felony for methamphetamine equipment
headings.reviewNote: Elevates paraphernalia possession to a class E felony if used or possessed in combination to manufacture amphetamines or methamphetamines.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for 579.074 covering drug paraphernalia possession elements, class D/A misdemeanor grading with section 558.021 pleading, and class E felony for amphetamine/methamphetamine manufacturing paraphernalia (L. 1989 S.B. 215 & 58 through A.L. 2014 S.B. 491; formerly 195.233; effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Offense of manufacturing drug paraphernalia defined
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits manufacturing with intent to deliver paraphernalia knowing or having reason to know it will be used for controlled substances.

headings.title: Misdemeanor classification and commercial felony enhancement
headings.reviewNote: Classifies paraphernalia manufacture as a class A misdemeanor, elevated to a class E felony if conducted for commercial purposes.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 579.076 covering unlawful manufacture of drug paraphernalia with intent to deliver and class A misdemeanor / commercial class E felony penalties (L. 1989 S.B. 215 & 58 through A.L. 2014 S.B. 491; formerly 195.235; effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Offense of possessing imitation controlled substances
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits knowingly possessing any imitation controlled substance.

headings.title: Class A misdemeanor penalty classification
headings.reviewNote: Designates possession of an imitation controlled substance as a class A misdemeanor.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 579.078 covering knowing possession of an imitation controlled substance and class A misdemeanor penalty (L. 1989 S.B. 215 & 58, A.L. 2014 S.B. 491; formerly 195.241; effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Offense of delivering imitation controlled substances
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits knowingly delivering, possessing with intent to deliver, or causing to be delivered any imitation controlled substance.

headings.title: Class E felony penalty classification
headings.reviewNote: Designates delivery of an imitation controlled substance as a class E felony.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 579.080 covering delivery or possession with intent to deliver an imitation controlled substance and class E felony penalty (L. 1989 S.B. 215 & 58, A.L. 2014 S.B. 491; formerly 195.242; effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Unlawful marketing of ephedrine or pseudoephedrine
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits marketing ephedrine or pseudoephedrine products for weight loss, appetite control, stimulation, or unapproved indications.

headings.title: Class E felony penalty classification
headings.reviewNote: Designates unlawful marketing of ephedrine or pseudoephedrine as a class E felony.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 579.082 covering unlawful marketing of ephedrine or pseudoephedrine for unapproved indications and class E felony penalty (L. 1996 H.B. 1301 & 1298, A.L. 2014 S.B. 491; formerly 195.248; effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Prohibited distribution without valid statutory registration
headings.reviewNote: Defines distribution in violation of registration requirements as knowingly distributing or dispensing in violation of section 195.030, outside registration authority, or knowingly refusing or failing to make, keep, or furnish section 195.050 records.

headings.title: Class E felony for distribution or dispensing violations
headings.reviewNote: Classifies violations of subdivision (1) or (2) of subsection 1 as a class E felony.

headings.title: Class A misdemeanor for recordkeeping violations
headings.reviewNote: Classifies violations of subdivision (3) of subsection 1 (recordkeeping and furnishing failures) as a class A misdemeanor.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for 579.084 (rewrote shifted subsections 2 and 3) covering registration and recordkeeping violations, class E felony for distribution/dispensing violations, and class A misdemeanor for recordkeeping violations (L. 1989 S.B. 215 & 58, A.L. 2014 S.B. 491; formerly 195.252; effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Unlawful delivery by manufacturer or distributor
headings.reviewNote: Defines unlawful delivery by a manufacturer, distributor, or employee as knowingly delivering a controlled substance while acting recklessly as to whether it will be used in violation of chapter 579.

headings.title: Class E felony penalty classification
headings.reviewNote: Designates unlawful delivery by a manufacturer or distributor as a class E felony.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 579.086 (corrected fabricated subsection 1 note) covering manufacturer or distributor knowing delivery while acting recklessly as to unlawful use and class E felony penalty (L. 1989 S.B. 215 & 58, A.L. 2014 S.B. 491; formerly 195.254; effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Pharmacist prescription tampering offense defined
headings.reviewNote: Defines prescription tampering by a chapter 338 licensed pharmacist as knowingly adulterating a prescribed drug's concentration or chemical structure without prescriber consent, or misrepresenting or selling a misbranded, altered, or diluted drug therapy to mislead.

headings.title: Class A felony penalty classification
headings.reviewNote: Classifies tampering with a prescription drug order as a class A felony.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 579.090 (rewrote fabricated subsection 1 note and corrected subsection 2 penalty from class E felony to class A felony) covering pharmacist adulteration, misrepresentation, or sale of diluted/altered prescription drugs and class A felony penalty (L. 2003 S.B. 5, A.L. 2014 S.B. 491; formerly 565.350; effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Prohibited possession of anhydrous ammonia
headings.reviewNote: Defines possession of anhydrous ammonia in a nonapproved container as possessing any quantity in a cylinder or portable container not conforming to 49 C.F.R. Parts 100 to 185 (as of Oct. 1, 2002) or not an approved tank truck, trailer, rail car, bulk tank, nurse tank, or applicator.

headings.title: Valve, fitting, hose materials, and UN 1005 labeling
headings.reviewNote: Requires anhydrous ammonia container valves, fittings, and hoses to be ammonia-resistant (prohibiting brass, copper, silver, or zinc) and requires conspicuous 'ANHYDROUS AMMONIA' or 'CAUTION: ANHYDROUS AMMONIA' and UN 1005 labeling.

headings.title: Class E felony penalty classification
headings.reviewNote: Designates unlawful possession of anhydrous ammonia in an unapproved container as a class E felony.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for 579.095 (rewrote fabricated subsection 2) covering possession of anhydrous ammonia in nonapproved DOT containers, valve/hose material and UN 1005 labeling standards, and class E felony penalty (L. 2001 H.B. 471 merged with S.B. 89 & 37 through A.L. 2014 S.B. 491; formerly 578.154; effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Definition of alcohol beverage vaporizer
headings.reviewNote: Defines 'alcohol beverage vaporizer' as any device capable of producing a breathable alcoholic beverage mixture for inhalation into the lungs.

headings.title: Prohibition on inducing symptoms with listed substances
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits intentionally or willfully inducing intoxication, euphoria, or sensory distortion by using or abusing listed solvents (including toluol), ethyl alcohol, or specified nitrites and iso-analogues.

headings.title: Exemption for FDA-approved and medical products
headings.reviewNote: Exempts FDA-approved therapeutic or over-the-counter drug products and substances lawfully administered under an authorized medical practitioner's order.

headings.title: Prohibited possession of solvents and nitrites
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits intentionally possessing solvents (particularly toluol) or specified nitrites and iso-analogues for use in the manner prohibited by sections 579.097 and 579.099.

headings.title: Prohibition on possessing or using alcohol vaporizers
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits any person from possessing or using an alcoholic beverage vaporizer.

headings.title: Preservation of legal liquor and beer consumption
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that nothing in this section prohibits the legal consumption of intoxicating liquor under section 311.020 or nonintoxicating beer.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 6 subsection headings for 579.099 (rewrote all 6 shifted/fabricated subsections) covering alcohol beverage vaporizer definition, prohibited symptom inducement, FDA/medical product exemption, prohibited solvent possession, vaporizer ban, and legal liquor/beer preservation (L. 1982 S.B. 522 §§ 3, 4 through A.L. 2014 S.B. 491; formerly 578.255; effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Purchasing solvents to assist unlawful inhalation
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits purchasing or possessing toxic chemical solvents with intent to deliver or aid another person in unlawful inhalation.

headings.title: Misdemeanor and repeat felony penalty classifications
headings.reviewNote: Classifies violating any provision of sections 579.097 to 579.101 as a class B misdemeanor for a first violation and a class E felony for any subsequent violation.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 579.101 (updated subsection 2 title/note to include repeat class E felony enhancement) covering possessing or buying solvents to aid others in violations and class B misdemeanor / class E felony repeat penalties for sections 579.097 to 579.101 (L. 1982 S.B. 522 §§ 5, 6 through A.L. 2014 S.B. 491; formerly 578.260; effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Unlawful sale of toxic solvents to induce intoxication
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits selling or transferring chemical solvents or nitrites knowing or intending the recipient will use them to induce intoxication.

headings.title: Sales prohibition for entertainment and alcohol businesses
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits businesses receiving over 50% income from alcohol or operating entertainment venues from selling volatile nitrites or toxic glue.

headings.title: Class D felony penalty classification
headings.reviewNote: Designates unlawful commercial or intentional sales of volatile solvents as a class D felony.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for 579.103 covering knowingly selling or transferring solvents to induce symptoms, alcohol/entertainment venue sales bans, and class D felony penalty (L. 1982 S.B. 522 §§ 7, 8 through A.L. 2014 S.B. 491; formerly 578.265; effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Maintaining premises for illegal drug activity defined
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits knowingly keeping or maintaining any building or structure used for illegal drug manufacture, storage, or repetitive drug use.

headings.title: Criminal indictment against owner or occupant
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes prosecuting attorneys to charge property owners, occupants, or both with maintaining a drug-related public nuisance.

headings.title: Class E felony penalty classification
headings.reviewNote: Designates keeping or maintaining a public nuisance under this section as a class E felony.

headings.title: Civil property forfeiture upon conviction
headings.reviewNote: Subjects buildings or structures maintaining drug nuisances to state civil forfeiture proceedings under sections 513.600 to 513.645.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsection headings for 579.105 covering drug-related public nuisance elements (excluding <=35g marijuana/synthetic cannabinoid), owner/occupant charging, class E felony grading, and civil forfeiture upon owner conviction (RSMo 1939 § 9844 through A.L. 2014 H.B. 1371; formerly 195.130; effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Lawful possession pursuant to valid prescription
headings.reviewNote: Protects lawful possession of controlled substances obtained directly from or pursuant to a valid medical prescription or practitioner's order.

headings.title: Defendant burden of proving statutory exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Establishes that pleadings need not negate statutory exceptions and places the burden of proof upon the defendant claiming authorization.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 579.107 covering lawful controlled substance possession pursuant to valid prescription or practitioner order and defendant burden of proving statutory exceptions (RSMo 1939 § 9849 through A.L. 2014 S.B. 491; formerly 195.180; effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Offense of possessing methamphetamine precursors defined
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits possessing precursor chemicals, reagents, or solvents with intent to manufacture amphetamines or methamphetamines.

headings.title: Prima facie evidence of manufacturing intent
headings.reviewNote: Establishes possession of more than twenty-four grams of ephedrine or pseudoephedrine as prima facie evidence of intent to violate this section, exempting practitioners and products possessed in legitimate business.

headings.title: Class E felony penalty classification
headings.reviewNote: Designates possession of methamphetamine precursors as a class E felony.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for 579.110 covering possession of methamphetamine precursors with manufacturing intent, 24-gram prima facie evidence with practitioner/business exception, and class E felony penalty (L. 1989 S.B. 215 & 58 through A.L. 2014 S.B. 491; formerly 195.420; effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Submission of federal suspicious transaction reports
headings.reviewNote: Requires drug wholesalers and manufacturers reporting suspicious ephedrine transactions to federal authorities to submit copies to local law enforcement.

headings.title: Statutory definition of suspicious transaction
headings.reviewNote: Defines suspicious transaction by incorporating federal reporting standards under 21 U.S.C. Section 830(b)(1).

headings.title: Class E felony penalty classification
headings.reviewNote: Designates failure to submit required suspicious transaction reports as a class E felony.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for 579.115 covering local law enforcement submission of federal suspicious transaction reports, 21 U.S.C. 830(b)(1) definition, and class E felony penalty (L. 2001 S.B. 89 & 37, A.L. 2014 S.B. 491; formerly 195.515; effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Distribution of non-controlled prescription medication prohibited
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits individuals under twenty-one from distributing non-controlled prescription drugs on school grounds or buses to unauthorized persons.

headings.title: Exemption for school nurses and emergency responders
headings.reviewNote: Exempts authorized school medical personnel and emergency responders administering medication during medical emergencies.

headings.title: Misdemeanor penalty classification and repeat enhancement
headings.reviewNote: Classifies distribution as a class B misdemeanor for a first offense, enhanced to a class A misdemeanor for subsequent convictions.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for 579.150 covering under-21 distribution of non-controlled prescription medication on school property or buses, school-authorized and emergency exemptions, and class B/A misdemeanor penalties (L. 2005 H.B. 353 & S.B. 254 through A.L. 2014 S.B. 491; formerly 577.625; effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Unauthorized possession of prescription medication prohibited
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits individuals under twenty-one from possessing non-controlled prescription medication on school property without a valid prescription.

headings.title: Exemption for authorized school staff and emergencies
headings.reviewNote: Exempts personnel authorized by school administrators to store or dispense medication and emergency personnel during emergencies.

headings.title: Misdemeanor penalty classification and repeat enhancement
headings.reviewNote: Classifies unauthorized possession as a class C misdemeanor for a first offense, elevated to a class B misdemeanor for subsequent convictions.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for 579.155 covering under-21 possession of non-controlled prescription medication on school property or buses, school-authorized and emergency exemptions, and class C/B misdemeanor penalties (L. 2005 H.B. 353 & S.B. 254 through A.L. 2014 S.B. 491; formerly 577.628; effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Definitions of prior and persistent drug offenders
headings.reviewNote: Defines prior drug offender (one prior felony drug finding) and persistent drug offender (two or more prior felony drug findings).

headings.title: Pleading and proof requirements for prior findings
headings.reviewNote: Requires prior findings of guilt to be pleaded and proven in accordance with procedures under section 558.021.

headings.title: Prohibition on jury sentencing for repeat offenders
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits instructing the jury on punishment ranges or allowing jury sentencing for prior or persistent drug offenders.

headings.title: Sentence enhancement for prior drug offenders
headings.reviewNote: Mandates sentencing a prior drug offender convicted of a class C, D, or E felony to the prison term for an offense one class higher.

headings.title: Sentence enhancement for persistent drug offenders
headings.reviewNote: Mandates sentencing a persistent drug offender convicted of a class C, D, or E felony to terms two classes higher, or class A for class B felonies.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 subsection headings for 579.170 covering prior and persistent drug offender definitions, section 558.021 pleading/proof, jury sentencing bar, and mandatory sentence enhancements (L. 1989 S.B. 215 & 58, A.L. 2014 S.B. 491; formerly 195.275; effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: State not required to negate statutory exemptions
headings.reviewNote: Establishes that the state is not required to negate any statutory exemption or exception in charging documents or trials, placing burden on claimant.

headings.title: Presumption of non-registration and defendant burden
headings.reviewNote: Establishes a statutory presumption against registration or order form authorization in the absence of affirmative proof produced by the defendant.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 579.180 covering state non-obligation to negate statutory exemptions and presumption of non-registration with claimant burden of production (L. 1989 S.B. 215 & 58, A.L. 2014 S.B. 491; formerly 195.367; effective 1-01-17).
